title: Pishon the camel driver
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yevamot 107b, Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai, “Did not Pishon the camel driver’s wife refuse the marriage in his absence?”

notes.text: The frozen locator is106b; the older machine reading has107b. The heading Gamal, “camel driver,” also differs from an indexed Namal alias. These remain source questions. Miyun is refusal by a minor girl to remain in an arranged marriage; she acted without her husband present.

The saved named Davidson Yevamot 107b paragraph contains the Beit Hillel/Beit Shammai exchange about Pishon’s wife performing miyun in his absence and spells הגמל. It supplies a match alongside source 106b and the older 107b reading, without proving Hyman’s folio glyphs or correcting the Namal alias. The wife remains the acting subject; all source variants remain visible.

Hyman (vol. III, p. 1010) prints Yevamot 107b (קז:) and the name Pishon HaGamal. The supplied Hebrew has 106b (קו:), and the catalog also has the alias HaNamal. The consulted Yevamot 107b has HaGamal and describes the wife’s refusal in her husband’s absence. Beit Shammai answer by invoking the way Pishon himself measured.
